speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower how the Ministry can improve the process by which workers, including foreign workers, can be protected against errant employers who do not insure them or compensate them for injuries and/or owe them their salaries.

speaker: Ms Kuik Shiao-Yin
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower (a) from 2012 to 2017, how many employers have been prosecuted in the Labour Court for respectively failing to compensate injured workers or insure them adequately; (b) what is being done to reduce the incidence of errant employers who ignore Labour Court orders and default on compensation for injured workers; and (c) how does the Ministry assist low-wage local and migrant workers who cannot afford further legal action to recover their unpaid wages.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The remaining 5% of the salary-related claims were unresolved because one of the employers has appealed the Labour Court order and the case is now with the High Court, eight are still in business but have yet to comply with their orders, while a vast majority − 199 out of 208 employers − had either ceased operations or faced impending business closure due to financial difficulties.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Therefore, out of the 208 employers, 199 either have closed down or are going to close down soon.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We are left with only nine employers, one of whom is appealing against the Labour Court order and eight have yet to comply with the orders.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: All these companies have been debarred from hiring foreign workers until they comply with the Labour Court orders.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The debarment also applies to culpable directors even if they were to start new companies.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We are also investigating those employers who are still in business because non-payment of salary is an offence under the Employment Act.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: While it is not our intention to criminalise every non-payment of salary, especially if it is the result of a business failure, we do prosecute serious or repeated cases for deterrence.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Such offences carry a fine of between $3,000 and $15,000 per charge, or imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months, or both.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: However, five out of about 16,000 cases did not because their employers had failed to purchase work injury compensation insurance and were unable to pay due to financial difficulties.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: MOM takes such offences seriously and prosecutes such employers under the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA) and debars the companies and individual directors from hiring foreign workers, until they compensate their workers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Such offences carry a maximum penalty of $10,000, or imprisonment of up to 12 months, or both.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is not because the employers could just ignore and refuse to pay up, but because they are mostly in deep financial difficulties, as I have explained earlier.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For cases where there is still some hope of enforcing the orders for unpaid salary or work injury compensation, the workers are required to apply for the Writ of Seizure and Sale through the State Courts.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is the same process that applies to all unpaid Civil Court orders, including those made by the State Courts.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In other words, the Labour Court orders are not less enforceable, compared to those issued or made by the State Courts.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: All civil claims have to go through the same process.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For those who need help, MOM assists the workers by advising them on the process and preparing the necessary documents.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Eligible low-wage local workers may seek legal assistance from the Legal Aid Bureau, whereas foreign workers may approach the Migrant Workers' Centre (MWC).

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Workers can also apply to the State Courts Registrar to waive or defer the costs of enforcing the order or to recover these costs from the sales proceeds.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Meanwhile, foreign workers with valid salary claims are also allowed to change employers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: More than 2,200 of such requests were granted in the past three years.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We will continue to strengthen our support for them.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Currently, foreign workers can already receive financial relief from MWC.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Likewise, for local low-wage workers, as announced in this House in August last year, those with unresolved salary claims will be able to receive short-term relief from the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) when it comes into operation in April this year.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As for workers with more serious injury, if they fail to receive their work injury compensation and are in financial difficulties, we will continue to assist them through the Workers' Fund managed by MOM.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: On the part of the workers, I urge them to bring their cases to MOM as early as possible.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This will greatly improve the chances of successfully resolving their claims before the employers reach dire financial straits.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I think there needs to be a lot more work to be done in communicating the slew of measures that the Minister had mentioned.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: For example, I think the Minister is familiar with the cases that were mentioned about the Bangladeshi workers who had been told to —

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: So, I would appreciate if the Minister could consider publicising the slew of measures a lot more.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: Can I just remind Members to keep your supplementary questions short?

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: There is no need to add long preambles to supplementary questions, please.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: And that is the reason why 99.9% of the cases had no problems.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Having said that, we do take such non-compliance seriously.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: That is why for every single case of non-compliance and non-payment, even for the first-time offender, MOM would prosecute the employer.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We do need to send a very clear message.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Of course, some may wonder why MOM cannot ensure 100% coverage.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Our challenge is that when a company purchases WICA coverage for its employees, the insurance policy does not go by name.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Along the way, during the year, there are workers who leave the company and workers who join the company.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As a result, the responsibility of making sure that workers are covered has to rest with the employer.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: It is impossible for MOM to comb through every WICA policy and to cross-check with the movement of staff, and so on.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Having said that, we want to assure this House that the compliance rate is high.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I also want to assure the House that we take every of these five cases very seriously.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For the information of this House, these five cases involve four foreign workers and one local worker.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: For the four foreign workers, we continue to pursue the cases, and one employer has just paid up and another case is now with the State Courts.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We are also helping the workers to find employment in Singapore and, at the same time, continue to find ways to resolve their outstanding claims.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In the case of the local worker, we have started actions to enforce the payment.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We are keeping track of these five cases to make sure that we derive the best outcome possible.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: In the case of the foreign workers mentioned by the Member, the media reports may have created a few misperceptions.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: First, the media reports said that the employers could just ignore and refuse to pay.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I want to assure this House that no employer can afford to ignore and refuse to pay.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As far as MOM is concerned, if I assess that this employer has the ability to pay, we will pursue it to the fullest.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I do not have to wait for the workers to enforce the order from the State Courts.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As MOM, I am already able to prosecute the employers because non-payment of salary, in itself, is an offence.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, I want to assure this House, please do not go away with the impression that any employer out there can afford to refuse and ignore the Labour Court orders.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I assure Members that this has never been the case and we will make sure it will never happen in the future.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Second, in this particular case, we did try very hard to help the worker.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The issue is that this worker has outstanding salary for 11 months.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The employer stopped paying him in October 2015 and it took him 11 months to come to MOM.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: By the time he came to MOM, the company was already in serious trouble.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The employer made an offer − paid each and every one of them $2,000 as a partial payment and, through the MWC, we offered to pay an ex-gratia payment of another $1,000.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The rest of it, the employer promised that he would pay up in instalments, through best effort.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Nine out of the 10 workers accepted this because they were realistic; they know the situation the company is in and they accepted it.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: At least two of them are now still working in Singapore with new employers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This particular claimant rejected the partial offer by the employer.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: He wanted to recover the full sum, which comes to about $7,500.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: As a result, he declined the offer by the employer.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We are now in the process of helping him to file the claim and enforce the Labour Court order, knowing that the chance of recovery is very slim.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I want to assure the House that we do take every case very seriously.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: What the workers can do, the best thing the workers can do to help themselves, is to come to us early.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Eleven months is too long to wait because by the time the employer has stopped paying you for 11 months, there is a high chance that the company is in deep financial difficulty.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: By and large, most workers will come to MOM after two to three months.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I also agree with Ms Denise Phua's point that we should step up more in terms of educating the employer, the workers and members of public that in Singapore, we do take the welfare of our workers − whether foreign or local − very seriously.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Compensation for work injury is very important because when the worker is injured, it may affect his ability to work.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: To not pay him the compensation is unacceptable.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: I want to assure this House that we will continue to strengthen the system.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Yes, I think the system today, by and large, is working well; 95% percent for unpaid salary and 99.9% for work injury, but I can assure this House that we will come up with more measures to link them up with MWC.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can I seek a clarification from the Minister?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: We are seeing some of those from our residents these days.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: They have noticed that for those employers who have their fair share of foreign workers as well as local, the foreign workers, ironically, have a sort of a safety milestone in the sense that when the employer decides to cancel their work pass, I think MOM will have to make sure that the employer pays them what is due to them, in terms of salaries and all that.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The shedding of foreign workers could come at an earlier stage whereas the local workers may continue to work in the firm.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Some of our residents are seeing that this payment of the foreign workers, their full packages and so on when their Work Permits are cancelled, this could be something risky for them as local employees will continue while the company's situation deteriorates.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I believe the Minister did mention he is alive to the situation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I would like to ask him whether the Ministry is reviewing this framework to, for example, have a mechanism in place that where you see an employer starting to cancel passes of foreign workers and so on, that the company is still able to make their payments to the local workers who remain with the company.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: What MOM does is this – we always encourage our workers, "The moment your employers stop paying you any salary, please come to us as early as you can".

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: This is our message and that remains our message.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Ms Lim may wish to advise her residents that anytime their employers stop paying them their salary, they can come to MOM straightaway.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: They do not have to wait for two or three months.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: The moment it is overdue, you have the right to exercise that option.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Moving forward, will MOM consider requiring all companies which employ Work Permit holders to place a security bond or a deposit with MOM, which can specifically be used when companies ignore the Labour Court orders for compensation to the workers?

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: Of that number, 28 of them were Work Permit holders with security bonds.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: We managed to get the security bond insurer to offer $2,000 to pay each of the workers.

speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
text: So, what Member Louis Ng mentioned is effectively already in practice today.
